record.original_question: Find practical criteria or methods for verifying polyconvexity and quasiconvexity for useful anisotropic stored-energy functions in nonlinear elasticity, especially beyond isotropic materials where the singular-value representation W(A)=Φ(v1,v2,v3) is available.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Are there ways of verifying polyconvexity and quasiconvexity for a useful class of anisotropic stored-energy functions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+\to \mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy function for a hyperelastic body, where $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ denotes the set of $3\times 3$ matrices with positive determinant. Recall the following notions:

(i) $W$ is polyconvex if there exists a convex function $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\times \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $W(A)=\Phi(A,\operatorname{cof} A,\det A)$ for all $A\in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$, where $\operatorname{cof} A$ is the cofactor matrix.

(ii) $W$ is quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) at $A\in\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ if for every bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^3$ and every $\varphi\in W_0^{1,\infty}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ with $A+\nabla\varphi\in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ a.e.,
$$\int_\Omega W(A+\nabla\varphi(x))\,dx \ge W(A)\,|\Omega|.$$

For an isotropic material, frame indifference and isotropy imply that $W$ admits the singular-value representation $W(A)=\Phi(v_1,v_2,v_3)$, where $v_1,v_2,v_3$ are the singular values of $A$, and this representation has been used to formulate verifiable conditions for polyconvexity and quasiconvexity.

Problem: Develop practical, verifiable criteria, or constructive methods, for deciding polyconvexity and quasiconvexity of stored-energy functions $W$ in the anisotropic setting—that is, when $W$ is invariant only under a proper subgroup $G\subsetneq SO(3)$ acting on the reference configuration (so the isotropic singular-value representation is not available)—covering a useful class of anisotropic materials (for instance transversely isotropic, orthotropic, cubic, tetragonal, trigonal, monoclinic, or triclinic symmetries).
artifact.category_tag: polyconvexity and quasiconvexity in nonlinear elasticity
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding practical criteria for polyconvexity and quasiconvexity of anisotropic stored-energy functions remains an active and largely open area. Partial constructions of polyconvex anisotropic energies based on structural tensors exist for transverse isotropy, orthotropy and cubic symmetry, while triclinic, monoclinic, tetragonal and trigonal cases remain problematic. Quasiconvexity in particular has no general verifiable criterion even in the isotropic case, and no systematic anisotropic treatment is known.

status_evidence.title: Design of Polyconvex Energy Functions for All Anisotropy Classes (V. Ebbing PhD thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Polyconvex energies based on structural tensors exist for transverse isotropy, orthotropy and cubic symmetry; well-known structural tensors for triclinic, monoclinic, tetragonal and trigonal energies were not useful so far.
status_evidence.claim: Anisotropic polyconvex construction is only partially understood; many symmetry classes remain open.

status_evidence.title: Construction of polyconvex, anisotropic free-energy functions
status_evidence.snippet: There exists no systematic treatment of anisotropic, polyconvex free energies in the literature.
status_evidence.claim: No systematic anisotropic polyconvexity theory is available.

status_evidence.title: Surface-Polyconvex Models for Soft Elastic Solids (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to address polyconvex modeling, indicating the question is active.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active research topic.
